case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 24th March, 2002 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4985 of 1999).
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J: This Appeal, by leave, is directed against the impugned judgment and order dated 24.03.2002 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4985 of 1999 discharging the Rule.

2. The case of the appellants, in brief, is that the pre-emptor-appellants filed pre-emption Case No. 8 of 1996 in the Court of the Additional Senior Assistant Judge, Mymensingh under Section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act, 1948 for pre-emption of 12-1/3 acres of land against the pre-emptee-respondent on the allegation, inter alia, that 14 acres of land of ROR Plot No. 274 appertaining to S.A. Khatian No. 131 was recorded in the name of Md. Shahed Ali who died leaving behind the pre-emptor-petitioners, Md. Shahidul Islam and others as heirs; that the pre-emptor Nos.1, 2 and 3 are the 2nd wife, a son and a daughter respectively of the said Md. Shahed Ali respectively and the said Md. Shahidul Islam is a son of the said Md. Shahed Ali; that by amicable partition amongst the heirs of the said Md. Shahed Ali, the pre-emptor-petitioners and the seller Md. Shahidul Islam got the said 14 acres of the case plot No. 274 by inheritance and they had been on joint possession of 14 acres in the case plot; that while the seller, Md. Shahidul Islam, son of the pre-emptor-petitioner No.1 and brother of the pre-emptor-petitioner Nos.2 and 3 had been owning and possessing 14 acres of land of the case plot in ejmali along with the pre-emptee respondent, a stranger to the case plot by a sale deed dated 03.07.1995 of TK. 60,000.00 without the knowledge of the pre-emptor-petitioners and that the pre-emptor-petitioners are co-sharers by inheritance in the case plot and as such they filed the pre-emption.

3. The pre-emptee-respondent contested the pre-emption case by filing written objections contending, inter alia, that the Md. Shahed Ali, predecessor of the pre-emptor-petitioners and seller, Md. Shaidul Islam, had 14 annas share and Saheran, mother of the said Md. Shahed Ali had 2 annas share in 14 acres of the case plot and accordingly S.A. Khatian No. 131 was finally published; that afterwards the said Shaeran died leaving behind son, Md. Shahed Ali, by amicable partition amongst the heirs of the said Md. Shahed Ali, the seller, Md. Shahidul Islam got the entire 14 acres of the plot and had been in possession of the same; that the seller, Md. Shahidul Islam requested the other co-sharers of the said Md. Shahed Ali to purchase the case land but all of them refused. Thereafter the seller, Md. Shahidul Islam requested the pre-emptee-respondent to purchase the case land who purchased the case land by a sale deed dated 03.07.1995 and he has been in possession of the case land since his purchase. Moreover, the pre-emptee-respondent made construction in the case land before the receipt of notice of the case.

4. Leave in the appeal was granted to consider the submissions of Mr. Abu Bakar Siddique, learned Advocate, appearing for the appellants that 14 acres of land of ROR Plot No. 274 appertaining to S.A. Khatin No. 131 marked exhibit-4 was recorded in the name of Md. Shahed Ali who died leaving behind the pre-emptor petitioners, Md. Shahidul Islam and others as heirs and this fact is admitted by the pre-emptee-respondent and that the learned Trial Court after scrutiny and on examination of the documents marked exhibit Nos. 1-4, held that the pre-emptor-petitioners are co-sharers in the case land and the petitioners proved their claim but the learned Judge of the High Court Division was totally wrong in not holding that the petitioners are co-sharers by inheritance in the case land. Mr. Sidduique further submits that the pre-emptor petitioners and the seller, Md. Shahidul Islam were in joint possession of 14 acres in the case plot and in the absence of any partition either amicable or by registered deed amongst the pre-emptor-petitioners and the seller, Md. Shahidul Islam and the pre-emptee-respondent having been failed to prove that the seller got 14 acres of the case plot in any way the pre-emptee case fails. Lastly Mr. Siddique submits that the pre-emptee-respondent O.P.W. No.1, Md. Matiur Rahman having stated in examination in chief that the dispute land by way of partition was obtained by Md. Shahidul Islam, son of Shahed Ali but in cross examination he totally contradicted himself by deposing that he cannot say how much land the pre-emptors got. Thereafter, he cannot also say in which plot Shahidul Islam got the land; further that he cannot say where and in what date the amicable partition took place and he will not be able to produce any paper and such a statement of the opposite party, O.P.W-1 having not been corroborated by any witness whatsoever or by circumstances of the case, the case of the pre-emptee fails. And the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division totally ignored and did not discuss the evidence of such material witness O.P No.1 resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice to the serious prejudice of the petitioners-appellants.

5. Mr. Abu Baker Siddique, learned Advocate, for the appellants strenuously supported the submissions which are the grounds for allowing the leave.

<u>6. Mr. Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate-on-record, appearing for the respondent submits that the learned Single Bench of the High Court Division after thorough analysis and assessment of pleadings, the evidences adduced by both parties found that the pre-emptor appellants are Locoparente with the pre-emptee-respondent and they played a definite role in signing about the disputed transaction and as such the appellants have lost their right of pre-emption by their estoppel and acquiescence. In support of this decision reported in 14 BLD (AD) 30, 50 DLR, 1998 HCD 616, 38 DLR 361. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, after proper consideration of the evidence, facts and circumstances of the case, found amicable partition in between the parties and thus correctly allowed the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 115 of 1997 and set aside the judgment and order dated 29.05.1997 passed in pre-emption case No. 8 of 1996 by the Senior Additional Assistant Judge, Mymensingh. Mr. Ali lastly submits that it reveals from observation and findings of Single Bench of the High Court Division that the prayer for pre-emption is barred by principle of estoppel and acquiescence.</u>

7. It appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that "Assuming that Shahidul has not disposed of the whole of the .14 acres of land of the case holding it can make any difference in establishing whether the petitioners co-sharers of the case holding. I say no, Shahidul has claimed exclusive ownership over the entire .14 acres of land of the case holding. The portion of land of the case holding which has not been disposed of by Shahidul my well remain with him exclusively. The effect of the partition would be that the other members of the family would not have any interest in land which has been apportioned to Shahidul by amicable partition."

<u>8. From the evidence on record it appears that said .14 acres of land was the property of late Md. Shahed Ali and after his death it descended upon his heirs. But it is the admitted case that the wives and children of late Md. Shahed Ali have amicably partitioned the land amongst themselves. The petitioners have not succeeded in proving by material evidence that they are co-sharers in the case holding. It is evidence that Md. Shahed Ali claimed excusive ownership over the entire .14 decimals of case land.</u>

9. In view of the above discussion and reasoning, we find no substance in the appeal.

10. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
